subject: biology-1
question: A couple has a child with **Down syndrome**, which results from trisomy 21. Which of the following events most directly explains how a gamete with two copies of chromosome 21 arose?

options.text: Crossing over exchanged a segment between chromosome 21 and a different chromosome.
Independent assortment placed both copies of chromosome 21 into one daughter cell.
A single gene on chromosome 21 duplicated itself during DNA replication.
Nondisjunction occurred, so homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids failed to separate and both copies of chromosome 21 went into one gamete.

explanation: Trisomy 21 requires a gamete that carries an extra chromosome 21, and the only way that forms is nondisjunction, a failure of homologs in meiosis I or of sister chromatids in meiosis II to separate. When such a gamete fuses with a normal gamete, the zygote has three copies of the chromosome. A and C cannot add a whole chromosome, and B mislabels the normal process of independent assortment as the cause.
